lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: I have knelt on that stone every morning for thirty years, and it is not there. It is in the quarry two valleys over, still in the ground. I walked through a drowned city this week and found it easier than this, because a city is somebody else's and that stone is mine.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: We bought the wall, and the wall bought us. Three centuries of my order standing on ground we were lent, and the charter I was raised on does not mention it once. I am going to be careful what I say to Ilse from here, because none of it is her fault and all of it will sound as though it is.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Poor and open. That is the order I joined, in those words, and I have just watched it be chosen rather than inherited. Thank you, Auditor. I am aware you did not technically do anything. I would like to thank you regardless.
